request.research_question: How does retrieval-augmented generation reduce hallucination and improve factuality in large language models?

plan.research_question: How does retrieval-augmented generation reduce hallucination and improve factuality in large language models?

queries.text: "retrieval-augmented generation" AND (hallucination OR factuality) AND "large language model"
queries.rationale: Directly targets research evaluating RAG in relation to hallucination and factuality in LLMs.

queries.text: ("retrieval-augmented generation" OR RAG) AND ("factual consistency" OR "faithfulness" OR "factual accuracy")
queries.rationale: Covers factuality evaluation terminology used beyond the word hallucination.

queries.text: ("retrieval grounding" OR "knowledge-grounded generation" OR "document-grounded generation") AND (hallucination OR "unsupported claims")
queries.rationale: Finds adjacent literature using alternative names for retrieval-supported generation and ungrounded outputs.

queries.text: ("large language models" OR LLMs) AND (retrieval OR "external knowledge") AND ("citation generation" OR "evidence attribution" OR "source attribution")
queries.rationale: Connects RAG with evidence attribution and citations, mechanisms that can improve verifiability and factual grounding.

queries.text: ("retrieval-augmented generation" OR "retrieval-augmented language model") AND ("retrieval quality" OR "retrieval relevance" OR "context quality") AND (hallucination OR factuality)
queries.rationale: Targets studies on how retrieval and retrieved-context quality affects hallucination and factual outcomes.
